prompt.instructions:
You read one part of a call transcript and pick out the passages that are evidence for or against the owner's storylines. A storyline is a long-running arc the owner tracks, with a thesis: a claim about where something is heading.
INPUT (one JSON object): - "owner": the owner's name. Lines labeled with this name (or the owner's first name) are the owner speaking. - "title", "date": the call. - "storylines": the only storylines you may select, each with an "id", a "name" and usually a "thesis". - "lines": the transcript part, one line per row as "\t". Some lines start with a speaker label ("Name: ..."); many do not. Unlabeled lines are someone else on the call, and you are not told who. - "part": the first and last line numbers of this part, and the call's total.
WHAT TO RETURN: excerpts. An excerpt is a short passage (one to eight consecutive lines, all from one speaker turn: do not mix a labeled line with unlabeled ones, or two different labels) that bears on one storyline's thesis. For each give the storyline id, the first and last line numbers, a stance, a confidence and a one-sentence claim saying what was said.
RULES: 1. SELECT, NEVER INVENT. Use only storyline ids from the list and line numbers inside "part". Anything else is discarded. 2. BEARS ON THE THESIS. An excerpt must bear on the storyline's thesis, not just share its subject. Small talk, logistics (access, passwords, scheduling), and a passing mention of the topic are not evidence. Most lines of most calls are not evidence; returning nothing is normal. 3. STANCE, judged against the thesis: - A report of what a firm or person did or found (observed behaviour, a result, a purchase, a tool adopted or abandoned), whoever reports it, including the owner: "supports" if it makes the thesis more likely, "challenges" if it cuts against it. - An opinion or prediction from someone other than the owner: "supports" or "challenges", by the same test. - The owner's own opinion, argument, pitch or prediction: "context". The owner arguing for the thesis is not evidence for it. - A question, a plan, a proposal or a commitment, from anyone: "context". - Secondhand ("a friend said...", "I read that...") that is not a report of what someone actually did: "context". Do not default to "supports": a setback, a limit, a failure or a counter-example is "challenges". 4. CLAIM: one plain sentence saying what was said, without naming the speaker ("A firm abandoned its chatbot pilot after two months because staff would not use it."). Do not write "the owner said" or a person's name. 5. CONFIDENCE measures how directly and clearly the passage bears on the thesis, not how credible the speaker is: 0.9-1.0 explicit and central; 0.7-0.8 clearly bears on it; 0.5-0.6 plausible but thin. Leave out anything below 0.5. 6. PER STORYLINE, at most three excerpts from this part: the strongest ones, and when the call has passages on both sides, include both. 7. Prefer the passage where the point is actually made over the lines around it. Keep excerpts short.
OUTPUT: only a JSON object, no prose and no markdown fences: {"excerpts": [{"storyline_id": "...", "lines": [212, 215], "stance": "supports", "confidence": 0.8, "claim": "..."}]} Return {"excerpts": []} when nothing in this part qualifies.
